items.reason: Go exposes /fast only when fast_mode is enabled and the current model catalog contains a tier named fast. It toggles using that tier's actual ID versus default, persists the config alias fast, propagates the effective ID to local and remote turns, and reports persistence success/failure like Rust. Canonical /btw, /multi-agents, and /quit popup entries remain separate from aliases.

Rust /clear dispatches ClearUi, which starts a fresh session while keeping the previous rollout resumable. Go TUI and interactive command paths now reset thread identity, transcript, and idle status instead of only clearing visible messages.

Runtime-backed slash commands now execute real actions: /app launches the Codex Desktop thread deep link, /rollout reads the active thread rollout path, /sandbox-add-read-dir validates and adds a readable root, /import invokes external-agent detect/import RPCs, and /memories opens a dedicated settings modal with persisted memory edits.

Go validates and emits ordered initialItems notifications, stores codexResponseHandoffMode, and routes streamed assistant output from appserver turns into bounded realtime handoff_append itemAdded notifications. Commentary/final channels, final-message prefix, UTF-8-safe head/tail truncation, and client-managed/codexResponsesAsItems skips are covered.

Go rollout loading and doctor inventory now accept .jsonl.zst, map compressed siblings to canonical .jsonl state-DB keys, prefer plain rollouts, and report corrupt compressed files without false stale rows.

Rust codex exec consumes app-server notifications and conditionally backfills turn/completed items. Go exec runs the agent directly and emits completed items from the active AgentLoopResult, so there is no cross-thread notification/backfill stage to filter.
items.userImpact: Only the active direct exec result can produce Go exec completion items; background app-server thread notifications are not part of this execution path and cannot pollute stdout.

items.reason: Go TUI startup receives locally prepared model metadata and permission requirements; it has no equivalent pair of remote model/list and configRequirements/read requests to parallelize. This is an architecture difference, not an unimplemented Go request scheduler.
items.userImpact: No additional startup round trips are introduced in the Go path; model and permission data are already available locally or from the existing settings load.

items.reason: Go detects external project Markdown memory, verifies SHA-256 content, imports under extension-scoped resources with scope.json and source/project/cwd/hash metadata, rejects path/hash failures, and removes resources for disappeared projects without inventing rollout provenance.
The Rust crate removal is repository-structure cleanup, not a wire-protocol removal.
items.userImpact: Go retains its existing realtime capability; external protocol behavior is unchanged.

items.reason: Linux Landlock/bwrap is verified on a native Kali runner. Native Windows platform and production ConPTY gates pass. Forty-seven relevant packages compile for Darwin/arm64, and Darwin network/sandbox vet plus actionlint pass. The macOS workflow now directly tests Keychain roots, a Unix-socket HTTP round trip, native seatbelt enforcement, and desktop/platform behavior; a native macOS workflow artifact is still required.

The opt-in Windows cancellation diagnostic reproducibly failed on Rust fa1d4c40d0: SDK abort left the PowerShell descendant running, created interrupted-marker.txt, and the resumed turn aborted. Go terminated the descendant, left no marker, and resumed successfully. This diagnostic remains excluded from the default differential set and is not used as evidence for the 25eecb071e baseline.
items.userImpact: Go cancellation is stronger on Windows: an interrupted command cannot continue mutating the workspace, and the thread remains resumable.

items.reason: All 82 Rust commits from fa1d4c40d0 through 25eecb071e were classified. Applicable protocol, MCP, executor sandbox, tool registry, remote compaction, telemetry, TUI width, OAuth redirect, serialization, fork boundary, and lifecycle changes are implemented with focused and race coverage; Rust-only dependency, release, allocation, and source-layout changes are explicitly classified.

items.reason: The official TypeScript SDK drives current Rust 25eecb071e and codex_go with isolated homes and workspaces, the configured default model, no SDK model overrides, strict event/item ordering, usage checks, and workspace side-effect comparison. The final approved suite passed 42 of 42 scenarios with zero mismatches or infrastructure failures; summary: sdktests/artifacts/suites/2026-07-30T164951300Z-parity/suite-summary.json. The model-free raw paginated fork audit also passed.
